title: 2014 USAMO Problem 1
statement: Let \(a,b,c,d\) be real numbers such that \(b-d \ge 5\) and all zeros \(x_1, x_2, x_3,\) and \(x_4\) of the polynomial \(P(x)=x^4+ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\) are real. Find the smallest value the product \((x_1^2+1)(x_2^2+1)(x_3^2+1)(x_4^2+1)\) can take.

solutions.text: Using the hint we turn the equation into $\prod_{k=1} ^4 (x_k-i)(x_k+i) \implies P(i)P(-i) \implies (b-d-1)^2 + (a-c)^2 \implies \boxed{16}$. This minimum is achieved when all the $x_i$ are equal to $1$.
